extracted.intended_audience: graduate students (Math 216) and readers learning foundations of algebraic geometry and homological algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Expository textbook material defining and giving criteria for adjoints, additive/abelian categories, kernels/cokernels, exactness, complexes, homology, (co)limits, flatness, and spectral sequences aimed at students of algebraic geometry/homological algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of adjunction via unit and counit
rubrics_metrics.description: Given functors F : A → B and G : B → A, natural transformations η : id_A → G F and ε : F G → id_B satisfying the identities G(ε_B) ◦ η_{G(B)} = id_{G(B)} for each B and ε_{F(A)} ◦ F(η_A) = id_{F(A)} for each A, then F is left-adjoint to G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These maps η (unit) and ε (counit) determine an adjunction; check the two triangular identities to verify adjointness. The left adjoint determines the right adjoint up to natural isomorphism, and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal property for groupification of an abelian semigroup
rubrics_metrics.description: A groupification of a semigroup S is a map of abelian semigroups π : S → G such that G is an abelian group and any map of abelian semigroups from S to any abelian group G' factors uniquely through π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a universal property: to construct the groupification H(S) one may take ordered pairs (a,b) in S thought of as a−b with an explicit equivalence relation; show the map S→H(S) satisfies the factoring property. Interpreting groupification as a left adjoint to the forgetful functor Ab → (abelian semigroups) clarifies the construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of additive category (Ad1, Ad2, Ad3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category C is additive if (Ad1) for each A,B in C, Mor(A,B) is an abelian group and composition distributes over addition; (Ad2) C has a zero object (initial and final); (Ad3) C has finite products (hence finite coproducts/direct sums).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In an additive category Hom is denoted Hom and morphisms are often called homomorphisms. Finite products are also finite coproducts (direct sums). Additive functors preserve the additive structure on Hom and send zero objects to zero objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of kernel and cokernel (universal property)
rubrics_metrics.description: A kernel of f : B → C is a morphism i : A → B with f ◦ i = 0 that is universal with respect to this property; dually a cokernel is defined by reversing arrows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kernels and cokernels are limits and colimits respectively; they are unique up to unique isomorphism. The kernel is not just an object but a morphism. Use the universal property to prove uniqueness and functorial behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: An abelian category is an additive category satisfying: (1) every map has a kernel and cokernel; (2) every monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel; (3) every epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From these three properties one can derive the usual behavior of kernels, cokernels, images, etc. In many parts of the text one can work concretely by interpreting examples as module categories rather than invoking the full abstract machinery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image of a morphism in an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: The image of f : A → B is defined as im(f) := ker(coker f) whenever this exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When im f exists, f factors uniquely through im f, and im f is a cokernel of ker f. In abelian categories these constructions behave as expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: complex, exactness at a term, and short exact sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence ... → A --f→ B --g→ C → ... is a complex at B if g ◦ f = 0. It is exact at B if ker g = im f. A short exact sequence is 0 → A → B → C → 0 (exact at every term).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exactness at B means the kernel of g equals the image of f (i.e., g has a kernel that is the image of f). Many standard facts reduce to checking exactness at terms. Examples: 0 → A → 0 exact iff A = 0; 0 → A --f→ B exact iff f is a monomorphism; 0 → A --f→ B --g→ 0 exact iff f is kernel of g and g is cokernel of f (i.e., isomorphism statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of homology of a complex
rubrics_metrics.description: If ... → A --f→ B --g→ C → ... is a complex at B, the homology at B is H := ker g / im f (equivalently the cokernel of im f → ker g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sequence is exact at B iff its homology at B is 0. Think of cycles = ker g and boundaries = im f, so homology = cycles mod boundaries. Indexing conventions (cohomology vs homology) depend on whether the complex is written with increasing or decreasing indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factorization of complexes into short exact sequences (relations among im, ker, coker, H)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complex A• can be 'factored' into short exact sequences: 0 → ker f_i → A_i → ker f_{i+1} → 0 and 0 → im f_i → A_{i+1} → coker f_i → 0 and further sequences relating im, ker, coker, and H_i(A•).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit sequences (1.6.5.3) and (1.6.5.4) express how homology sits between kernels, images, and cokernels; these are useful for proving long exact sequences and other standard homological arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence in cohomology from short exact sequence of complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: A short exact sequence of complexes 0• → A• → B• → C• → 0 induces a long exact sequence ... → H^{i-1}(C•) → H^i(A•) → H^i(B•) → H^i(C•) → H^{i+1}(A•) → ... with a natural connecting homomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The connecting homomorphism is natural; standard proofs use the Snake Lemma or explicit diagram chases. This is core to the notion of derived functors and spectral sequence arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of right-exact, left-exact, and exact functors
rubrics_metrics.description: A covariant additive functor F between abelian categories is right-exact if exactness A' → A → A'' → 0 implies F(A') → F(A) → F(A'') → 0 is exact. Dually, F is left-exact if 0 → A' → A → A'' implies 0 → F(A') → F(A) → F(A'') is exact. A functor is exact if it is both left- and right-exact. Contravariant versions are defined by reversing arrows appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact functors preserve exact sequences; left-exactness and right-exactness determine where derived functors (e.g., R^iF or L_iF) will appear. Examples and exercises illustrate behavior for Hom and tensor functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization is exact and flatness
rubrics_metrics.description: Localization of A-modules at a multiplicative set S, i.e., S^{-1}(-), is an exact covariant functor. Consequently S^{-1}A is a flat A-algebra. More generally, a module N is flat iff - ⊗_A N is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exactness of localization to deduce that taking cohomology commutes with localization. Exercise 1.6.F asks to prove localization is exact; Exercise 1.6.G relates Hom and localization for finitely presented modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: FHHF theorem (interaction of homology and exactness of functors)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a covariant functor F between abelian categories and a complex C•: (a) If F is right-exact there is a natural morphism F(H_i(C•)) → H_i(F(C•)). (b) If F is left-exact there is a natural morphism H_i(F(C•)) → F(H_i(C•)). (c) If F is exact these morphisms are inverses and hence isomorphisms, so F commutes with homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the natural maps using coker/ker/exactness properties (hint given). The special case of tensoring with a module N motivates flatness: if -⊗N is exact then it commutes with homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoints and (co)limits imply exactness properties
rubrics_metrics.description: If (F,G) is an adjoint pair then F commutes with colimits and G commutes with limits. In abelian categories kernels are limits and cokernels are colimits; hence right adjoints and limits are left-exact, and left adjoints and colimits are right-exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequently, right adjoints preserve kernels (left-exact) and left adjoints preserve cokernels (right-exact). Use these facts to deduce exactness behavior of common adjoint functors (e.g., restriction/extension of scalars, π_* and π^* etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Freyd–Mitchell embedding justification for diagram chasing
rubrics_metrics.description: If C is an abelian category with Hom(X,Y) a set for all X,Y, then there exists a ring A and an exact, fully faithful functor embedding C into Mod_A, allowing one to justify elementwise diagram chases by working in a module category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invoking the full theorem is uncomfortable, Mac Lane's 'elementary rules for chasing diagrams' provide an alternative justification. The embedding theorem allows one to reduce abstract arguments to concrete module computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered colimits and limits: exactness statements and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: In Mod_A, colimits over filtered index categories are exact. However, in general abelian categories filtered colimits need not be exact (counterexamples exist via dualization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working in module categories one can use exactness of filtered colimits to commute colimits with homology (Exercise 1.6.L). Exercise 1.6.K asks to show filtered colimits are exact in Mod_A; a cautionary counterexample is given for Ab with Z → Z/(p^n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and construction of double complexes and total complex
rubrics_metrics.description: A double complex is a collection of modules E^{p,q} with horizontal maps d→ : E^{p,q} → E^{p+1,q} and vertical maps d↑ : E^{p,q} → E^{p,q+1} satisfying d→^2 = 0, d↑^2 = 0 and the squares anticommute (or commute after sign changes). The total complex E• is given by E^k = ⊕_{p+q=k} E^{p,q} with differential d = d→ + d↑ and d^2 = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions: first index = column, second = row; anticommute vs commute is a sign convention. The total complex's cohomology is the hypercohomology of the double complex. Variations (e.g., first quadrant) simplify spectral sequence convergence behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate definition of spectral sequence from a double complex
rubrics_metrics.description: A spectral sequence (rightward orientation) consists of pages E^r_{p,q} (r = 0,1,2,...) with differentials d^r_{p,q}: E^r_{p,q} → E^r_{p-r+1,q+r} satisfying (d^r)^2 = 0 and E^{r+1}_{p,q} ≅ H(E^r_{p,q}, d^r). The 0th differential is the rightward one (d^0 = horizontal differential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ep,q^r is a subquotient of Ep,q^{i} for i < r. For first quadrant double complexes, for fixed (p,q) the pages stabilize for large r and compute pieces of the total cohomology; one uses these pages to compute/coarsely approximate the cohomology of the total complex.
